processing.description: Read the text of the article's version-of-record PDF (sha256 f41eb020a2b6…, the copy the authors deposited on Zenodo). Found each of 21 sentences from the abstract and section 3 word for word on its page before publishing; a minus sign had to match a minus sign.

Published the mean, the median and the range across the reviewed studies for the 28 options whose values the text states, exactly as printed. Values listed with several options are read in the order the options are named; 'between A and B' is the range across studies. Each value's sentence is in its note.

Where the article states one value twice with different numbers, the value is null and both statements are given.

processing.description: Read the WORLD row of mortality_region_2019_ref.xlsx (the reference model run) and of mortality_region_2019_noFF.xlsx (the run with all fossil-fuel emissions removed) from the Edmond deposit of Lelieveld et al. 2023: column 'NCD+LRI+LRI5-+CPO3', excess deaths in 2019 from all causes due to outdoor fine particles and ozone. Checked that both files list the same regions with the same population, and that the reference total and its 95% confidence limits round to the paper's printed 8.34 million (5.63, 11.19 million).

Subtracted the deaths without fossil fuels from those of the reference run, in exact decimal arithmetic on the stored values: the deaths the paper attributes to fossil-fuel emissions. Confidence limits cannot be subtracted, so no range is calculated; the observation quotes the paper's own 95% confidence interval.

scope.basis: Modelled excess deaths from all causes due to long-term exposure to outdoor fine particles (PM2.5) and ozone in 2019: exposure from the EMAC atmospheric chemistry model (2019 emissions and meteorology) combined with NASA satellite-based fine particles and population, and deaths from Burnett and colleagues' FUSION relative-risk model applied to Global Burden of Disease 2019 baseline mortality. Deaths from fossil fuels are the reference run less a run with every fossil-fuel emission removed at once. The authors give three reasons their estimate is higher than most earlier ones: the new relative-risk model, counting deaths from all causes as well as from specific diseases, and the large fall in exposure when fossil fuels are removed entirely.

scope.basis: Carbon dioxide budget from the start of 2026 (1 January 2026) for 1.5 °C above 1850–1900, 50% likelihood considering only uncertainty in the transient climate response to cumulative emissions (TCRE); rounded by IGCC to the nearest 10 GtCO₂. processing.description: Read the Historical Global Shares API response (sha256 9ad0752d138d…, retrieved 2026-10-04): 4318 records, 1990–2023, 127 income slices a year. Checked for every year that the slices run from 0 to 100% of people with no gap or overlap, that each slice's width matches its label, and that the emission shares add up to 1 (within one billionth).

Kept 1990–2022 and left out 2023. SEI's national inputs are consumption-based up to 2022 and territorial (where emissions happen) from 2023, so later shares are not comparable. The API's own national values show the break (historicalDataByCountry, NatEmisions as served, rounded here to the tonne; snapshots retrieved 2026-10-05): Switzerland 121,979,300 t in 2022 and 32,737,300 t in 2023 (sha256 e23373e0dc56…); the United States 5,642,856,100 t in 2022 and 4,911,391,000 t in 2023 (sha256 ed93564c2981…); the United Kingdom 488,532,000 t in 2022 and 305,146,300 t in 2023 (sha256 fde2cd775620…). The 2023 values match Global Carbon Budget 2025 territorial emissions, not consumption (research of 2026-10-05, docs/research/sources-ghg-food-personal-2026-10-05.json).

For each year, added up the EmissionShare of the slices in each group with exact decimal arithmetic on the values as served: the poorest 50% (slices up to the 50th percentile), the richest 10% (from the 90th) and the richest 1% (from the 99th, which SEI splits into finer slices). The richest 1% are part of the richest 10%.
Multiplied by 100 to give percent.

scope.basis: Fossil carbon dioxide only, consumption-based (territorial emissions plus net emissions embodied in trade); other greenhouse gases and land-use change are not included. Each country's emissions are shared among its people in proportion to income between a floor and a ceiling (SEI's elasticity of 1). SEI's pages do not say how international aviation and shipping are allocated.

provenance.description: Estimated number of people, in millions, living on land below the local once-a-year coastal flood level (the high-tide line plus the local 1-year flood height), at today's sea level and with the sea levels projected for 2050 and 2100 under low (RCP2.6), moderate (RCP4.5) and high (RCP8.5) emissions, from Supplementary Data 1 of Kulp & Strauss (2019), using the CoastalDEM elevation model. Projected values give the median and the 5th to 95th percentile range of the sea-level projections. Two projection sets are published side by side, never mixed: K14 (Kopp et al. 2014), which the paper calls probabilistic and closely aligned with IPCC findings and which gives the abstract's lead figure (below high tide by 2100 under low emissions); and K17 (Kopp et al. 2017), which adds unstable Antarctic ice, is not probabilistic, and gives the abstract's high-end figures. Both predate the IPCC's Sixth Assessment Report. The population is held at its 2010 distribution (LandScan 2010), so future values show where today's people live relative to future seas, not projected populations. The method is a bathtub model that ignores sea walls and other defences, so it measures exposure, not flooding.

processing.description: Read Supplementary Data 1 (sha256 37a6ab2fc25e…): its 27 column headings had to be exactly as expected. Kept the 13 rows of Place 'World' (present day, then K14 and K17 under RCP2.6, 4.5 and 8.5 for 2050 and 2100), whose Total is 6800 million people, and from each only the three CoastalDEM columns of RL1: land below the future local high tide line plus the local 1-year coastal flood level. The SRTM, JAXA and MERITDEM columns and the SIDS and country rows are not used here (the country rows are published, in people, by the indicators ending '-by-country').

Published the 50th percentile as the value and the 5th and 95th percentiles as the lower and upper ends of a 90% interval, exactly as printed in millions of people (nothing rounded or recalculated). The present-day row prints '--' for both percentiles, so it has no range.

Dated the present-day row 2010, the year of the LandScan population that every row counts (its sea level is that of 2000, the zero of both projection sets), and the projected rows 2050 and 2100, the years of their sea levels; the population stays as it was in 2010.

Published both projection sets as values of the 'projection' dimension, side by side and never mixed, because the abstract uses both: its 190 M (150–250 M) below high tide by 2100 under low emissions is K14 (K17 gives another range), and its 'up to 630 M' and 'up to 340 M' below the annual flood level by 2100 and mid-century are K17's 95th percentiles under RCP8.5. Checked both, and the present day's 110 M and 250 M, against these cells.

Checked the file against Table 1 of the corrected article (sha256 912692e7c7a3…, page 3): each of its 24 CoastalDEM totals, median and 90% interval, equals the file's three numbers. Found the 20 sentences that the scope and the cross-checks rely on, each on its page of the article (which page 1 marks 'Corrected: Author correction'), and the 2 on units, exposures and percentiles in the description of the supplementary files (sha256 2b98673da602…).

scope.basis: Below the local mean higher-high water line plus the local once-a-year coastal flood height (Global Tides and Surge Reanalysis), after the given sea-level rise. People are counted where they lived in 2010 (LandScan 2010); population growth and migration are not modelled. Land cut off from the sea is left out. Present day is the sea level of 2000, the zero of both projection sets. 2050 and 2100 add the median and the 5th to 95th percentiles of the sea-level rise projected by Kopp et al. 2014 (K14) or Kopp et al. 2017 (K17, unstable Antarctic ice) under RCP2.6, 4.5 and 8.5, projections made before the IPCC's Sixth Assessment Report. A bathtub model: sea walls, levees and other defences are not counted (levee locations are not available globally), so protected coasts such as the Netherlands are included. It measures exposure, not flooding.
scope.geography: World: land between 56° south and 60° north, where CoastalDEM is defined, home to 99.7% of the world's population in 2010

provenance.description: How many times people were forced to leave their homes, staying within their own country, because of floods, storms, wildfires, landslides, droughts and other weather-related disasters, worldwide, each year since 2008, by hazard. Calculated from IDMC's event data by adding up IDMC's estimate for each event with a reported figure. These are movements, not people: one person displaced twice is counted twice, and pre-emptive evacuations are included. IDMC records far more events than it did as monitoring and reporting widened (its file has 1,044 weather-related event rows for 2008 and 7,064 for 2025), so a rise is not evidence that disasters are becoming more frequent. The figures are weather-related; they are not attributed to climate change. For 2008 and 2010–2016, IDMC gives China's displacement as one figure a year that is not split by hazard, so it is not in those years' sums and they are not comparable with later ones; each year's note gives the figures left out. 701 weather-related event rows in this release have no reported figure and are left out, not counted as zero. Totals printed in IDMC's Global Report on Internal Displacement are built differently and are not used.

processing.description: Read the sheet '1_Disaster_Displacement_data' of IDMC's GIDD disaster export (README: last update 2026-08-31, extracted 2026-10-05; recorded 2026-10-12, sha256 25c78f150cff…): 44,335 rows for 2008–2025, one per disaster event in a country and year.

Kept the 41,821 rows whose Hazard Category is 'Weather related' (IDMC's own category, CRED EM-DAT classification). Left out 2,084 'Geophysical' rows (earthquakes, volcanic activity and dry mass movement) and 430 'Mixed disasters' rows (displacement IDMC does not assign to one hazard). For China, IDMC gives one 'Mixed disasters' row a year in 2008 and 2010–2016, so China's displacement in those years is not in the sums; nothing is estimated in its place. 'Mixed disasters' figures left out, by year: 2008 26,822,000; 2009 130,000; 2010 18,584,000; 2011 9,402,232; 2012 11,135,953; 2013 12,168,639; 2014 6,150,513; 2015 6,444,000; 2016 9,143,000; 2024 19,132; 2025 531,353; each year's total carries a note with them.

Added up the raw figure (Disaster Internal Displacements (Raw)) of these rows by Year, the year IDMC reports the displacement in, and by IDMC's Hazard Type, and over all nine types, as whole numbers. The rounded column is not used.

Left out the 701 weather-related rows with no reported figure; they are never counted as zero, and each value whose rows include some carries a note with their number. Rows with a figure and without one, by year: 2008 1,044/0; 2009 1,576/1; 2010 1,609/0; 2011 1,655/2; 2012 1,675/3; 2013 2,065/65; 2014 2,362/42; 2015 1,877/5; 2016 2,182/26; 2017 867/0; 2018 1,548/0; 2019 1,835/32; 2020 1,796/25; 2021 1,176/368; 2022 2,263/16; 2023 3,774/57; 2024 4,778/33; 2025 7,038/26.
A hazard type with no row in a year has no value for that year. No check against the totals printed in IDMC's Global Report on Internal Displacement: they are built differently and are not used.

scope.basis: IDMC's estimates of internal displacements (forced movements within a country, pre-emptive evacuations included) for disaster events whose Hazard Category is 'Weather related' (CRED EM-DAT classification), added up by the year IDMC reports them in and by IDMC's Hazard Type. Geophysical events (earthquakes, volcanic activity, dry mass movement) and IDMC's 'Mixed disasters' (displacement not assigned to one hazard, including China's yearly figure for 2008 and 2010–2016) are left out. Mass movement here is landslides, wet mass movement and avalanches; extreme temperature is cold waves and heat waves. Only events with a reported figure are counted. Displacement by drought, which builds up slowly, is harder to monitor than displacement by sudden events. Weather-related, not attributed to climate change.

processing.description: Read the sheet 'Global Carbon Budget' of Global_Carbon_Budget_2025_v1.0.xlsx (Global Carbon Budget 2025 v1.0, ICOS object qSjPBsV1drZnYdH-yCJMmkGn): one row per year 1959–2024, in billion tonnes of carbon per year. Sinks are positive numbers in the sheet and stay positive here.

Checked the sheet's definition of the budget imbalance on every year: fossil emissions plus land-use change emissions, minus atmospheric growth, ocean sink, land sink and cement carbonation sink, equals the imbalance column (largest difference 3.3e-14 GtC/yr). This confirms that the fossil column is before the cement carbonation sink is subtracted.

Converted from billion tonnes of carbon to billion tonnes of carbon dioxide by multiplying by 3.664, the factor the sheet states ("multiply the numbers below by 3.664"), with exact decimal arithmetic on the stored values.

Lower and upper are given for two components only, from the one-sigma uncertainties the sheet states: ±5 % of fossil emissions, and ±0.7 billion tonnes of carbon (2.5648 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide) per year for land-use change. The sheet gives the ocean sink (±0.4) and land sink (±0.5 billion tonnes of carbon per year) uncertainties only 'on average' and atmospheric growth's as 'variable', so those components and the imbalance have no range.

scope.basis: Carbon dioxide only. Fossil emissions are before the cement carbonation sink is subtracted; sinks are positive numbers. Land-use change is the average of three bookkeeping models (BLUE, OSCAR, LUCE); the ocean and land sinks are model and data-product averages.

processing.description: Read INTL.txt from EIA's bulk file INTL.zip. EIA's bulk manifest gives the INTL release as last updated 30 September 2026 and names this zip as its file, so the vintage is 'Sep 2026'. The zip was last modified on the server on Sat, 03 Oct 2026 09:49:21 GMT.

Kept the annual consumption series in quadrillion Btu: total energy consumption and its five fuels (coal, natural gas, petroleum and other liquids, nuclear, renewables and other), checking each series' name and units. Kept the World and the 220 countries and territories in pipeline/geo/entities.csv, matched by EIA's ISO 3 code (EIA's XKS is Kosovo, KOS, and its SCG, Former Serbia and Montenegro, is Serbia and Montenegro as reported together, SRB_MNE); EIA's regional aggregates are left out, and so are these geographies, which have no entity in the crosswalk: Former Czechoslovakia; Former U.S.S.R.; Former Yugoslavia; Germany, East; Germany, West; Hawaiian Trade Zone; Netherlands Antilles; U.S. Pacific Islands; U.S. Territories; Wake Island.

Checked EIA's accounting method against its own generation series: for every country other than the United States, the energy content of hydro, wind, solar, geothermal and tide and wave electricity is 3,412 Btu per kilowatt-hour, the captured-energy approach (11,140 country-years checked). Not on that basis in this file: USA: 72 values, e.g. solar 2023 3676, solar 2024 3622 Btu per kWh. World nuclear consumption is 10,379 Btu per kilowatt-hour of nuclear generation in 2024, the heat input of the plants.
Where EIA's total differs from the sum of its five fuel series, both are published as given. Entities where they differ in this vintage: USA, WLD (World 2024: total minus the sum is -1.442 quad Btu).
EIA's codes '--', 'NA' and 'ie' (which the file does not define) are null values whose reason quotes the code.

Fossil share = (coal + natural gas + petroleum and other liquids) / total energy consumption x 100, for each entity and year with all four values (exact decimal arithmetic on EIA's values). A share above 100% carries a note with both numbers.

scope.basis: Primary energy consumption as EIA accounts for it: fossil fuels at their heat content; electricity from hydro, wind, solar, geothermal and tide and wave power at its own energy content, 3,412 Btu per kilowatt-hour (the captured-energy approach; EIA's United States series depart from it for solar and geothermal); nuclear at the heat input of the plants. Not comparable with totals from the Energy Institute or the IEA, which count non-combustible electricity differently. 'Renewables and other' is EIA's own category and can be negative. Fossil fuels are EIA's coal, natural gas, and petroleum and other liquids; the denominator is EIA's total energy consumption.
scope.geography: Countries and territories, and the world

processing.description: Read the IEA Global EV Data Explorer's historical file from api.iea.org/evs (fetched 2026-10-05, sha256 43de47975d08…), which carries no version label; its latest year is 2025, the year the Global EV Outlook 2026 reports on.

Kept the 'EV sales share' rows (category Historical, powertrain EV: battery-electric and plug-in hybrid together; unit percent) for cars, vans, buses, trucks and two- and three-wheelers, 2010–2025. The 26,007 car price rows (price_* and sales-historical-price-data), based on S&P Global Mobility data that the IEA's licence does not cover, were not read.

Matched IEA region names to countries in pipeline/geo/entities.csv by name (Czech Republic, Korea, Lao PDR, Turkiye, USA and Viet Nam by declared alias). The IEA's regional groupings were left out because the file does not list their members: Advanced Economies, Africa, Asia Pacific, Developing Economies excl. China, Europe, European Union, Latin America, Middle East and Caspian, Southeast Asia.
Published each value as the shortest decimal that reproduces the single-precision number stored in the file (for example 0.012 for 0.012000000104308128).
Left as null, with the reason, every value above 100%, which cannot be a share of sales. In this vintage: ARE vans 2021; ARE vans 2022; ARE vans 2023; ARE vans 2024; ARE vans 2025.
Found the report's statement of the 2025 world share for cars on page 16 of the PDF.

provenance.description: How hot the hottest day of the year gets over land: each place's highest daily maximum temperature of the year, averaged over all land except Antarctica, as the difference from its 1961–1990 average, each year from 1950. From the ERA5 reanalysis (a weather model constrained by observations, not a direct measurement; values before the satellite era rest on fewer observations), as calculated by Indicators of Global Climate Change 2025. It measures intensity, how hot the hottest day is, not how often extremes happen, and it shows the change without attributing it to a cause. IGCC adds a single 0.51 °C to express it relative to 1850–1900; that is not added here. IGCC's Berkeley Earth and HadEX3 versions are not included: they are not coverage-matched with ERA5, Berkeley Earth's terms are non-commercial, and HadEX3 ends in 2018.

provenance.description: How many times as often an extreme that came once in 10 years (or once in 50) in the second half of the 19th century (1851–1900 for heat and rain, 1850–1900 for drought), a climate without human influence, occurs at global warming levels of 1, 1.5, 2, 3 and 4 °C: the hottest day of the year over land (once-in-10 and once-in-50-year events), the wettest day of the year over land, and agricultural and ecological drought in the regions projected to dry. Modelled: the median of the CMIP6 climate models assessed for Figure SPM.6 of the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (2021), with the 5–95% range the figure shows (a range reaching below 1 includes no increase at all). These are model estimates for each level of warming, not counts of observed events, and a warming level is not a year: every value is dated 2021, the year of the assessment. The published figure labels the 1 °C level 'Present'; the world has warmed further since, so 1 °C is not today's warming, and nothing between levels is interpolated. The 3 °C level is in the data but not in the published figure. Drought covers 16 drying regions, not the whole world.

processing.description: Read the four frequency files of Figure SPM.6 (CEDA version v20210809: panel_a/TXx_freq_change_10_year_event.csv, panel_b/TXx_freq_change_50_year_event.csv, panel_c/Rx1day_freq_change_10_year_event.csv, panel_d/drought_freq_change_10_year_event.csv). Each gives, at global warming levels of 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 °C, how many times as often an extreme that occurred once in 10 (or 50) years in 1850–1900 occurs: the median of the CMIP6 multi-model ensemble and its 17th, 83rd, 5th and 95th percentiles. Checked that the five percentiles are in order in every row.

Published the median as the value and the 5th to 95th percentile as the range (very likely range), as the published figure shows them; the 17th–83rd percentiles are not published. Values are as printed in the files. Each is dated 2021, the year of the assessment: the warming level, not the date, is what varies. The 3.0 °C level is in the files but not in the published figure, whose caption lists 1, 1.5, 2 and 4 °C; its label says so.

Checked against metadata.yaml: each file is listed under its figure panel (the Readme's panel letters for precipitation and drought are out of date); the caption gives the base periods used in the labels (1851–1900 for heat and rain, 1850–1900 for drought); and it lists 17 drying regions for drought, of which the Caribbean is not included in the calculation, so the drought values cover 16.

Checked against the published figure (IPCC AR6 WGI SPM, p. 18): each of the 16 ranges it prints equals the 5th and 95th percentiles rounded half up to one decimal, and each printed median is a publisher cross-check.

scope.baseline: 1851–1900 (heat and rain) or 1850–1900 (drought)
scope.basis: CMIP6 multi-model ensemble under several SSP scenarios, at global warming levels relative to 1850–1900; extremes defined at model grid-box scale. Value: the ensemble median; range: its 5th to 95th percentile (very likely range), as in the published figure. Projected changes in the IPCC's words, including at 1 °C; dated 2021, the year of the assessment.
scope.geography: Global land for the hottest and the wettest day of the year. For drought, the AR6 regions projected to dry: the caption lists 17 (W. and C. North America, N. and S. Central America, the Caribbean, N., N.E., S.W. and S. South America, the South American Monsoon, West and Central Europe, the Mediterranean, W. and E. Southern Africa, Madagascar, E. and S. Australia) and the Caribbean is not included in the calculation, so 16.

unit.label: times as often as in the second half of the 19th century

provenance.description: Of the 45 inhabited regions the IPCC uses, how many have seen an increase, a decrease, low agreement in the type of change, or too little data and literature to say, in hot extremes, heavy precipitation and agricultural and ecological drought from the 1950s to 2021, as assessed in the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (2021, Figure SPM.3). Increases are split by the IPCC's confidence that human influence contributed: high, medium, or low because studies disagree. Calculated by counting the regions in the IPCC data; the totals of each type of change match the counts printed on the published figure, and the split by confidence is counted from the same data. Regions differ in size and population, and each is assessed as a whole. 'Limited data' and 'low agreement' mean the evidence is missing or mixed, not that nothing changed, and a confidence level says how sure the IPCC is that people contributed, not how large the contribution was.

processing.description: Read the three panel files of Figure SPM.3 (CEDA version v20221116: SPM3_panel_a.csv, SPM3_panel_b.csv, SPM3_panel_c.csv), BADC-CSV, one row per region. Checked that each has the 45 inhabited AR6 regions listed in its comments, once each, the same in all three; that all three say 'years 1950 to 2021' and that each region is assessed as a whole for the 1950s to the present. Every count is dated 1950/2021.

Counted the regions in each type of observed change (Increase, Decrease, Low agreement in the type of change, Limited data and/or literature), and split the increases by the confidence in a human contribution (High, Medium, Low due to limited agreement), using the producer's labels. The files word the low-agreement category as SPM3_panel_a.csv 'Low agreement in type of change'; SPM3_panel_b.csv 'Low agreement in the type of change'; SPM3_panel_c.csv 'Low agreement in the type of change'; each is read as the printed figure's 'Low agreement in the type of change'. Checked that the four types add up to the regions and the split adds up to the increases. No region is weighted by area or population.

Checked the pairings the split relies on: every region with low agreement in the type of change has 'Low due to limited agreement' confidence, every region with limited data has 'Low due to limited evidence', and every increase has High, Medium or 'Low due to limited agreement'. Regions with a decrease, and their confidence: agricultural and ecological drought: NAU (Low due to limited agreement).

Checked against the published figure (IPCC AR6 WGI SPM, p. 10): the count of each type of change printed beside its legend is a publisher cross-check. The split of increases by confidence is not printed there; it is counted from the IPCC data.

scope.basis: Counts of the IPCC AR6 WGI reference regions in each assessed category, for the world; no regional values are published. Expert assessment of observed change since the 1950s (files: years 1950 to 2021), each region as a whole. Categories and labels are the IPCC's; only counts are computed.

processing.description: Read World_Census_Agriculture_E_All_Data_(Normalized).csv from FAOSTAT's WCAD bulk zip. The vintage is the domain's DateUpdate, 27 April 2026, from FAOSTAT's bulk-download catalogue (datasets_E.json), whose entry names this zip and gives FileRows 28,565, the number of data rows in this file. The zip was last modified on the server on Fri, 19 Jun 2026 13:54:45 GMT.

Kept the rows of item 27002 "Holdings" (element 60850 "Number") and of FAO's 16 land-size items (elements 60850 "Number" and 50260 "Area", in hectares), for every country and census in the WCA rounds 1930 to 2020. Values are published as printed, one per country and census, with the census year as the period (split years such as "2015/16" and ranges such as "2018-2021" written as 2015/2016 and 2018/2021) and the WCA round, census year as printed, FAO's flag and FAO's note in each value's note.

Nothing is added up: there is no world or regional total, because each country's census is of a different year and countries define a holding in their own way, and the land-size classes, which differ between countries and partly nest, are not summed. No census in this file reports a class together with a class nested in it.

Left out former states and territories reported only before their dissolution, with no entity here (Czechoslovakia, Yugoslav SFR); FAO regional and analytical groups (China). Their values are never re-assigned to other entities.
FAO reports China's census rows under area 351 "China" (M49 159), which FAOSTAT's area standard uses for China including Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan; they are not assigned to mainland China (CHN).
Flags in the rows used: A "Official figure" (7,311 values); I "Value imputed by a receiving agency" (3,274 values); each value's note names its flag.

scope.basis: Agricultural holdings counted in each country's census of agriculture, as compiled by FAO for the World Census of Agriculture (WCA) rounds 1930 to 2020. Each value is one census; the period is the census year, and each value's note gives the WCA round and FAO's note on how the country defines a holding (countries set their own minimum size limits and scope, which affects comparisons between countries). No world or regional total. Land-size classes are FAO's, as named in its item list (for example "0-<1"); countries report different sets of classes, some classes contain others (2 to under 5 contains 2 to under 3, 3 to under 4 and 4 to under 5), and the classes are never added up here. The item names state no unit for the classes.
scope.geography: Countries and territories, each in its own census years

Values are published as printed, one per country and census, with the census year as the period (split years such as "2015/16" and ranges such as "2018-2021" written as 2015/2016 and 2018/2021) and the WCA round, census year as printed, FAO's flag and FAO's note in each value's note.

Nothing is added up: there is no world or regional total, because each country's census is of a different year and countries define a holding in their own way, and the land-size classes, which differ between countries and partly nest, are not summed. No census in this file reports a class together with a class nested in it.

FAO reports China's census rows under area 351 "China" (M49 159), which FAOSTAT's area standard uses for China including Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan; they are not assigned to mainland China (CHN).
Flags in the rows used: A "Official figure" (7,311 values); I "Value imputed by a receiving agency" (3,274 values); each value's note names its flag.

scope.basis: Agricultural holdings counted in each country's census of agriculture, as compiled by FAO for the World Census of Agriculture (WCA) rounds 1930 to 2020. No world or regional total. Land-size classes are FAO's, as named in its item list (for example "0-<1"); countries report different sets of classes, some classes contain others (2 to under 5 contains 2 to under 3, 3 to under 4 and 4 to under 5), and the classes are never added up here. Checked, in all 9,174 areas and years from 1990 where FAO prints them (FAO's regions included), that "Agrifood systems" equals the sum of the three stages and each stage equals the sum of its processes present, to within 0.01 kilotonnes. Nothing is computed from this check; it shows that the parts published are FAO's whole total, with no remainder.

Left out FAO's projections for 2030 and 2050, which the file flags F ("Forecast value").
Published the 22 process items, 1990–2023, each value exactly as one row of the file.

Left out former states and territories reported only before their dissolution, with no entity here (Belgium-Luxembourg, Czechoslovakia, Ethiopia PDR, Netherlands Antilles (former), Pacific Islands Trust Territory, Sudan (former), USSR, Yugoslav SFR); FAO regional and analytical groups (Africa, Americas, Annex I countries, Asia, Australia and New Zealand, Caribbean, Central America, Central Asia, China, Eastern Africa, Eastern Asia, Eastern Europe, Europe, Land Locked Developing Countries (LLDCs), Latin America and the Caribbean, Least Developed Countries (LDCs), Low Income Food Deficit Countries (LIFDCs), Melanesia, Micronesia, Middle Africa, Net Food Importing Developing Countries (NFIDCs), Non-Annex I countries, Northern Africa, Northern America, Northern Europe, OECD, Oceania, Polynesia, Small Island Developing States (SIDS), South America, South-eastern Asia, Southern Africa, Southern Asia, Southern Europe, Western Africa, Western Asia, Western Europe); the European Union (27), a region (only the world and countries and territories are published). Their values are never re-assigned to other entities.
Converted kilotonnes to million tonnes by dividing by 1,000 (exact decimal arithmetic on the printed values).
Every value used carries FAO's flag E, which the file's codebook defines as "Estimated value".

Labelled FAO's items in plain words: "Farm gate" as "On the farm"; "Land-use change" as "Clearing land for farming"; "Pre- and post-production" as "Before and after the farm"; "Enteric Fermentation" as "Farm animals' digestion (burps)"; "Manure Management" as "Storing and handling manure"; "Manure left on Pasture" as "Manure left on grazing land"; "Manure applied to Soils" as "Manure spread on fields"; "Synthetic Fertilizers" as "Synthetic fertiliser on fields"; "Rice Cultivation" as "Flooded rice fields"; "Crop Residues" as "Crop leftovers rotting on fields"; "Burning - Crop residues" as "Burning crop leftovers"; "Drained organic soils" as "Drained peat soils"; "On-farm energy use" as "Fuel and electricity used on farms"; "Savanna fires" as "Grassland (savanna) fires"; "Net Forest conversion" as "Cutting down forests"; "Fires in humid tropical forests" as "Tropical forest fires"; "Fires in organic soils" as "Peat fires"; "Fertilizers Manufacturing" as "Making fertiliser"; "Pesticides Manufacturing" as "Making pesticides"; "Food Processing" as "Processing food"; "Food Packaging" as "Packaging"; "Food Transport" as "Transport"; "Food Retail" as "Shops"; "Food Household Consumption" as "Cooking and storing food at home"; "Agrifood Systems Waste Disposal" as "Disposing of food waste". Only the names shown differ; every value is FAO's item of that name.

scope.basis: The 22 FAOSTAT process items of item "Agrifood systems" (6518), with FAO's names, each under its stage; overlapping FAOSTAT items (Emissions from livestock, Emissions from crops, Emissions on agricultural land, IPCC Agriculture, AFOLU, LULUCF) are not included, so nothing is counted twice. A few synthetic-fertilizer values are negative as published (Somalia and Timor-Leste, some years). FAO TIER 1 estimates for every country with the same method, not country inventory submissions, so they can differ from a country's own inventory. Farm gate is FAO's grouping: it includes on-farm energy use, drained organic soils and savanna fires as well as livestock and crop emissions. Land-use change counts only what FAO attributes to agriculture: net forest conversion (deforestation) plus fires in humid tropical forests and in organic soils (peat). The carbon taken up by standing forests (FAOSTAT item "Forestland", a net removal) is outside FAO's agrifood total: it is not subtracted and not shown. Net forest conversion uses FAO Forest Resources Assessment period averages, so it is constant within each assessment period and steps between periods, including a method break between 2000 and 2001; year-to-year changes in land-use change are partly an artefact of that method. Pre- and post-production covers fertilizer and pesticide manufacturing, food processing, packaging, transport, retail, household consumption (cooking, storing) and agrifood waste disposal. International aviation and shipping bunkers are a separate FAOSTAT item and are not included. Stage totals start in 1990.

provenance.description: Methane and nitrous oxide emitted on farms each year since 1961 in producing each of 14 farm products, for the world and each country, in carbon dioxide equivalent, as allocated by FAO. Counts only emissions on the farm from: methane from animals' digestion (enteric fermentation) and from manure management; nitrous oxide from manure management, from manure applied to soils and from manure left on pasture; and, for rice and other cereals, nitrous oxide from crop residues and from synthetic fertiliser, methane and nitrous oxide from burning crop residues, plus methane from flooded rice paddies. Not counted: energy used on farms, drained organic (peat) soils, savanna fires, clearing land (land-use change), and everything before and after the farm (making fertiliser and feed, processing, packaging, transport, retail, cooking and waste). Only 14 products: meat of cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats, pigs and chickens; raw milk of cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats and camels; hen eggs; rice; and other cereals together. Soy, palm oil, fruit, vegetables, sugar, pulses, fish and other farm animals are not covered, so the products do not add up to food's emissions. These are farm-gate values, not life-cycle footprints: FAO says they should not be compared with life-cycle assessment figures. FAO's split of sheep, goat, buffalo and camel emissions between meat and milk makes 75 meat values negative in the February 2026 release, all goat, buffalo or sheep meat and most of them in Mali and Bhutan, down to about -6.3 million tonnes for goat meat in Mali in 2011. They are published as printed.

provenance.description: Methane and nitrous oxide emitted on farms per kilogram of each of 14 farm products, each year since 1961, for the world and each country, in kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent, as published by FAO (the product's farm emissions divided by its production). The kilogram is FAO's production weight: carcass weight for meat (FAO's items are meat 'with the bone'), raw whole milk, eggs in shell and harvested cereals. It is not a kilogram of boneless meat or of food as bought, so these values are not comparable with retail or life-cycle figures per kilogram of food. Counts only emissions on the farm from: methane from animals' digestion (enteric fermentation) and from manure management; nitrous oxide from manure management, from manure applied to soils and from manure left on pasture; and, for rice and other cereals, nitrous oxide from crop residues and from synthetic fertiliser, methane and nitrous oxide from burning crop residues, plus methane from flooded rice paddies. Not counted: energy used on farms, drained organic (peat) soils, savanna fires, clearing land (land-use change), and everything before and after the farm (making fertiliser and feed, processing, packaging, transport, retail, cooking and waste). Only 14 products: meat of cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats, pigs and chickens; raw milk of cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats and camels; hen eggs; rice; and other cereals together. Soy, palm oil, fruit, vegetables, sugar, pulses, fish and other farm animals are not covered, so the products do not add up to food's emissions. These are farm-gate values, not life-cycle footprints: FAO says they should not be compared with life-cycle assessment figures. Where a country produces little of a product the value can be very large, and where FAO gives no production figure there is no value. FAO's split of sheep, goat, buffalo and camel emissions between meat and milk makes 72 meat values negative in the February 2026 release, most of them in Mali and Bhutan, down to about -854 kilograms per kilogram for goat meat in Mali in 2010. They are published as printed.

provenance.description: The UK's whole consumption-based greenhouse gas footprint in the latest year of Defra's release, split into the 14 broad categories of end use Defra publishes for that year only, in million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent. The first eleven are households' spending and their direct emissions from heating and driving; 'Central and local government', 'Gross fixed capital formation' (investment, including buying houses) and 'Other' (charities, valuables, inventories) are not. Flights have no row of their own: households' spending on flights is inside 'Transportation', while business and government travel sits in the supply chains of the other rows. Health and education paid for by government are under government. The rows add up to the published total. Defra revises earlier years in every annual release. UK only.

provenance.description: The consumption-based greenhouse gas footprint of an average person in Sweden: emissions in Sweden and abroad from producing everything used in Sweden, divided by the population, in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent per person per year, as published by Naturvårdsverket from Statistics Sweden's official statistics. Split into the six parts the producer publishes. Four are household consumption (transport, food products, housing, and other goods and services); the page does not say whether meals eaten out count under food products or under other goods and services. The other two, public consumption (schools, hospitals, agencies) and investment (buildings including new homes, machinery, computers, valuables and changes in inventories), are shared out per person but are not personal choices; buying a new home counts under investment, not housing. The parts are rounded by the producer and may differ from the published total by 0.01 t. International flights are undercounted: only jet fuel bought in Sweden is counted, without stopovers or the high-altitude effect. The page shows the IPCC Fourth Assessment Report (AR4) global warming potentials (methane 25, nitrous oxide 298) in a general conversion table, without saying they apply to this series. Sweden only; it is not a world average or a measure of any one person.

Checked the page heading, the responsible authority (SCB), the axis title, the series names and the CSV header before reading any value.

Selected the six parts as published, each with its Swedish column name kept in its label: Transporter = transport; Livsmedel = food; Boende = housing; Övrigt = other-household; Offentlig konsumtion = public-consumption; Investeringar = investment. Checked that in every year the six parts add up to the published Totalt within 0.01 t (the producer rounds each value to two decimals). Years where they differ by 0.01 t: 2009 (+0.01 t), 2010 (+0.01 t), 2020 (+0.01 t), 2021 (-0.01 t), 2022 (-0.01 t). No value was changed.

Checked the page's tab 'Koldioxidekvivalenter': its general conversion table ('Omräkningstabell') gives CO2 1, CH4 25 and N2O 298, the IPCC Fourth Assessment Report (AR4) 100-year values, and links that report ('Koldioxidekvivalenter för ytterligare växthusgaser i IPCC:s fjärde utvärderingsrapport'), but the page does not say that this series uses them. So no global warming potential is recorded in the scope; the basis says what the page shows.

processing.description: Checked that each file read (ERF_best_aggregates.csv, ERF_p05_aggregates.csv, ERF_p95_aggregates.csv) is byte-identical to the same path inside the IGCC-2025a release zip deposited on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21494229, sha256 04658ff91053…).

Read the best estimate, 5th and 95th percentile of effective radiative forcing for each year from 1750 and each of 18 agents and aggregates, as published (W/m²). The 5–95% range is IGCC's, taken from its own percentile files; nothing is re-estimated.

Checked that every human-caused column is exactly zero in 1750 in all three files, so its values are the change since 1750. Solar and volcanic forcing are not zero in 1750 (best estimates 0.02159121 and 0.234943996 W/m²), so the natural and total values are IGCC's time series as published, not changes since 1750. IGCC gives solar for 2025 as a single-year value, separate from its assessment over complete solar cycles, and includes volcanic forcing in the time series without a single-year assessment for 2025 (ESSD Sect. 5).

Checked in the best-estimate file that each aggregate equals the sum of its parts to 1e-6 W/m² (aerosols, well-mixed greenhouse gases, total human-caused, natural, total), which confirms what each column means. Not published as agents of their own: minor, nonco2wmghg, anthro_nonwmghg, which are sums of published columns (non-CO₂ well-mixed greenhouse gases = methane + nitrous oxide + halogenated gases; minor = contrails + land use + black carbon on snow + stratospheric water vapour; human-caused other than well-mixed greenhouse gases = ozone + stratospheric water vapour + aerosols + contrails + land use + black carbon on snow), checked to 1e-6 W/m² the same way.

scope.baseline: 1750 for every human-caused agent (each is zero in 1750 in IGCC's files); solar and volcanic as in IGCC's time series, which are not zero in 1750
scope.basis: IGCC's ERF time series 1750–2025 (ESSD Fig. 5b), single-year values. Solar is IGCC's single-year solar ERF, separate from its assessment over complete solar cycles; volcanic is included in the time series, though IGCC gives no single-year volcanic assessment for 2025. Natural and total include both. 5th to 95th percentile range from IGCC's ensemble.
scope.geography: Global mean

indicators.title: Effective radiative forcing by agent, 1750–2025 (IGCC 2025)

processing.description: Read FRA_Years_2026-10-11.csv from the FRA 2025 platform's bulk download (all countries and areas). The vintage is the download date in the member names, 2026-10-11; the platform has no other version label.

Kept 1a_forestArea (forest area, thousand hectares, as printed) and its flag for 236 countries and areas and the six reporting years 1990, 2000, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2025. Flags: A "Normal value, official data reported by country/area" (194 countries and areas); I "Imputed value, desk study, data compiled by FAO" (42 countries and areas); each country's values name their flag in a note.
Matched each country and area by its ISO 3 code; French Guiana, Mayotte, Réunion and Svalbard and Jan Mayen Islands, which FRA reports separately, are published as their own entities.
World = the sum of the forest area of all 236 countries and areas in the file for each year (exact decimal arithmetic), as FAO computes its global figure.

For comparison only, the WORLD row of the report's Table 5 (PDF page 35, published 2025-10-21), in thousand ha: 1990: report 4 343 534, here 4 343 534.45; 2000: report 4 236 587, here 4 236 589.39; 2010: report 4 201 001, here 4 200 995.20; 2015: report 4 181 435, here 4 181 439.67; 2020: report 4 165 241, here 4 165 289.00; 2025: report 4 140 217, here 4 140 443.71. The two differ slightly; the platform data can include country revisions made after the report was published.

Kept 1a_forestArea (forest area, thousand hectares, as printed) and its flag for 236 countries and areas and the six reporting years 1990, 2000, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2025. Flags: A "Normal value, official data reported by country/area" (194 countries and areas); I "Imputed value, desk study, data compiled by FAO" (42 countries and areas); each country's values name their flag in a note.
Matched each country and area by its ISO 3 code; French Guiana, Mayotte, Réunion and Svalbard and Jan Mayen Islands, which FRA reports separately, are published as their own entities.
World = the sum of the forest area of all 236 countries and areas in the file for each year (exact decimal arithmetic), as FAO computes its global figure.

Annual net change for each interval between reporting years = (forest area at the end − forest area at the start) / the number of years, in thousand hectares per year (exact decimal arithmetic); negative values are net loss. The report defines forest area net change the same way, as the difference in forest area between two points in time.

For comparison only, the WORLD row of the report's Table 6 (PDF page 36) gives the annual net change as −10 695 thousand ha a year for 1990–2000 (here −10 694.51) and −4 122 for 2015–2025 (from the platform data used here, −4 099.60; that 10-year interval is published here as 2015–2020 and 2020–2025). The platform data can include country revisions made after the report was published.

Net change = (forest area at the end of the interval − at its start) / years in the interval. Net change is not deforestation: gains elsewhere offset part of the forest lost.

scope.basis: Tree cover loss: stand-replacing disturbance, or the complete removal of tree cover canopy, of vegetation taller than 5 m, mapped each year from Landsat at 30 m (Hansen/UMD, Global Forest Change v1.13), where tree canopy cover was at least 30 percent in 2000. Primary forest: the 2001 extent of humid tropical primary forest (Turubanova et al. 2018); loss outside the humid tropics is not counted.
scope.geography: Countries and territories (GADM's country codes, mapped to ISO 3166-1) and the world, which also includes areas GADM codes separately (XAD, Z01, Z06, Z07). Only countries with humid tropical primary forest have rows.

World: read loss-global-annual (the same query without the country grouping), 2001–2025. Checked that the countries, with the codes left out below, add up to it exactly in every year, for all loss and for loss due to fire.
Not published as countries: GADM codes with no entity in our table (XAD 80 ha; Z01 4,365 ha; Z06 555 ha; Z07 164,532 ha, all years together). Their loss is included in the world totals.

scope.basis: Tree cover loss: stand-replacing disturbance, or the complete removal of tree cover canopy, of vegetation taller than 5 m, mapped each year from Landsat at 30 m (Hansen/UMD, Global Forest Change v1.13), where tree canopy cover was at least 30 percent in 2000. Loss due to fire: UMD/GLAD (Tyukavina et al. 2022), a part of all loss.
scope.geography: Countries and territories (GADM's country codes, mapped to ISO 3166-1) and the world, which also includes areas GADM codes separately (XAD, Z01, Z06, Z07).

processing.description: Read loss-drivers-country-annual: WRI's table gadm__tcl__iso_change v20260424 queried through the Global Forest Watch Data API with the SQL in the file's URL (https://data-api.globalforestwatch.org/dataset/gadm__tcl__iso_change/v20260424/download/csv?sql=SELECT%20iso%2C%20wri_google_tree_cover_loss_drivers__driver%2C%20umd_tree_cover_loss__year%2C%20SUM%28umd_tree_cover_loss__ha%29%20AS%20umd_tree_cover_loss__ha%20FROM%20data%20WHERE%20umd_tree_cover_density_2000__threshold%20%3D%2030%20GROUP%20BY%20iso%2C%20wri_google_tree_cover_loss_drivers__driver%2C%20umd_tree_cover_loss__year%20ORDER%20BY%20iso%2C%20wri_google_tree_cover_loss_drivers__driver%2C%20umd_tree_cover_loss__year), at a tree canopy cover in 2000 of at least 30 percent. Hectares as in the file, not rounded.
A country and year with no row in the file has no loss recorded for it; nothing is filled in.

Driver classes as WRI names them; "Hard commodities" is labelled "Mining and energy (hard commodities)" and "Settlements & Infrastructure" "Settlements and infrastructure". Each 1 km cell's loss is assigned to its one dominant driver (WRI/Google DeepMind, Sims et al. 2025).
World: the sum of every row of the file by year and driver, including the codes left out below. Checked that the drivers add up to loss-global-annual in every year, to within 0.01 ha.
Not published as countries: GADM codes with no entity in our table (XAD 80 ha; Z01 4,365 ha; Z06 555 ha; Z07 164,532 ha, all years together). Their loss is included in the world totals.

scope.basis: Tree cover loss: stand-replacing disturbance, or the complete removal of tree cover canopy, of vegetation taller than 5 m, mapped each year from Landsat at 30 m (Hansen/UMD, Global Forest Change v1.13), where tree canopy cover was at least 30 percent in 2000. Loss is not deforestation: it includes plantation harvest, fire and natural disturbance, and regrowth is not subtracted. Method changes from 2011 and 2015 make early and late years less comparable. Drivers: the dominant driver of loss in each 1 km cell, 2001–2025, from a model trained on labelled samples (WRI/Google DeepMind, Sims et al. 2025). WRI counts permanent agriculture, hard commodities and settlements and infrastructure as permanent conversion to another land use; the other drivers are usually followed by regrowth.
scope.geography: Countries and territories (GADM's country codes, mapped to ISO 3166-1) and the world, which also includes areas GADM codes separately (XAD, Z01, Z06, Z07).

provenance.description: Days a year with a heat index of 39 °C or more, 1995–2014 as the models simulate it and projected for 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under low, middle and very high emissions, for every country and territory, from the CMIP6 climate models as bias-corrected, downscaled and aggregated by the World Bank's Climate Change Knowledge Portal. Each value is averaged over the land of the place, not weighted by where people live. The value is the median of the models and the range runs from the 10th to the 90th percentile of the models. The 1995–2014 values are the models' simulation of the recent past, not observations.

processing.description: Read CCKP's 39 CMIP6 0.25° all_countries_subnationals files of hi39 (climatology): the multi-model ensemble median, 10th and 90th percentiles for the 1995–2014 historical runs and 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Every file holds the same 246 countries and 3,528 regions.

Checked every country's value against its own regions' values in the same file: within the lowest and highest region (±0.01, rounding), or equal to its one region. It holds for every country in every file.

Published every country and territory (246), mapping CCKP's codes to the site's entities (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes as they are, KSV, CCKP's code for Kosovo, as KOS): the median as the value and the 10th and 90th percentiles as the range, as printed, with the 20-year window as the period and the emissions scenario as a dimension.

processing.description: Read CCKP's 39 CMIP6 0.25° all_countries_subnationals files of hi39 (climatology): the multi-model ensemble median, 10th and 90th percentiles for the 1995–2014 historical runs and 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Every file holds the same 246 countries and 3,528 regions.

Checked every country's value against its own regions' values in the same file: within the lowest and highest region (±0.01, rounding), or equal to its one region. It holds for every country in every file.

Published 3,493 states, provinces and other first-level regions under CCKP's own codes, leaving out the 32 DIS.* units (areas the World Bank assigns to no country), and the 3 units CCKP lists under China for Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan (CHN.147295925 'Taiwan Sheng'; CHN.1491879 'Macau, SAR'; CHN.33364910 'Hong Kong, SAR'), places this site publishes under their own codes: the median as the value and the 10th and 90th percentiles as the range, as printed, with the 20-year window as the period and the emissions scenario as a dimension.

scope.basis: CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (bias-corrected and downscaled to 0.25° by CCKP): the median of the models, with their 10th–90th percentile as the range. Days with a heat index of 39 °C or more (CCKP's hi39). The heat index, as the US National Weather Service defines it, is how hot it feels once humidity is counted. 20-year averages: 1995–2014 from the historical runs; 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Projections, not forecasts of any one year.
scope.geography: Each state, province or other first-level region as CCKP draws it on the World Bank's official boundaries: the area-weighted mean of the 0.25° grid cells inside it, averaged over the land, not weighted by where people live. Left out: the 32 areas the World Bank assigns to no country, and the three units CCKP lists under China for Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, places with their own values in the country indicator, and their own region where CCKP lists one.

processing.description: Read CCKP's 39 CMIP6 0.25° all_countries_subnationals files of hd35 (climatology): the multi-model ensemble median, 10th and 90th percentiles for the 1995–2014 historical runs and 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Every file holds the same 246 countries and 3,527 regions.

Checked every country's value against its own regions' values in the same file: within the lowest and highest region (±0.01, rounding), or equal to its one region. It holds for every country in every file.

Published every country and territory (246), mapping CCKP's codes to the site's entities (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes as they are, KSV, CCKP's code for Kosovo, as KOS): the median as the value and the 10th and 90th percentiles as the range, as printed, with the 20-year window as the period and the emissions scenario as a dimension.

scope.basis: CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (bias-corrected and downscaled to 0.25° by CCKP): the median of the models, with their 10th–90th percentile as the range. Days with a daily maximum temperature of 35 °C or more (CCKP's hd35, Tmax >= 35 °C). 20-year averages: 1995–2014 from the historical runs; 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Projections, not forecasts of any one year.
scope.geography: Each country or territory as drawn by the World Bank's official boundaries: the area-weighted mean of the 0.25° grid cells inside it, averaged over the land, not weighted by where people live. No world value.

indicators.title: Days a year at 35 °C or more by country, projected for 20-year windows to 2099 (CMIP6, World Bank CCKP)

unit.label: days a year with a daily maximum temperature of 35 °C or more

provenance.attribution: The World Bank: Climate Change Knowledge Portal: Observed Climate Data, ERA5 0.25-Degree (doi:10.57966/128g-6s70): Copernicus Climate Change Service ERA5. The World Bank: Climate Change Knowledge Portal: Projected Climate Data, CMIP6 0.25-Degree (doi:10.57966/b54h-7s87): CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (World Climate Research Programme).
provenance.description: Days a year at 35 °C or more, 1995–2014 as the models simulate it and projected for 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under low, middle and very high emissions, for every state or province, from the CMIP6 climate models as bias-corrected, downscaled and aggregated by the World Bank's Climate Change Knowledge Portal. Each value is averaged over the land of the place, not weighted by where people live. The value is the median of the models and the range runs from the 10th to the 90th percentile of the models. The 1995–2014 values are the models' simulation of the recent past, not observations.

processing.description: Read CCKP's 39 CMIP6 0.25° all_countries_subnationals files of hd35 (climatology): the multi-model ensemble median, 10th and 90th percentiles for the 1995–2014 historical runs and 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Every file holds the same 246 countries and 3,527 regions.

Checked every country's value against its own regions' values in the same file: within the lowest and highest region (±0.01, rounding), or equal to its one region. It holds for every country in every file.

Published 3,492 states, provinces and other first-level regions under CCKP's own codes, leaving out the 32 DIS.* units (areas the World Bank assigns to no country), and the 3 units CCKP lists under China for Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan (CHN.147295925 'Taiwan Sheng'; CHN.1491879 'Macau, SAR'; CHN.33364910 'Hong Kong, SAR'), places this site publishes under their own codes: the median as the value and the 10th and 90th percentiles as the range, as printed, with the 20-year window as the period and the emissions scenario as a dimension.

scope.basis: CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (bias-corrected and downscaled to 0.25° by CCKP): the median of the models, with their 10th–90th percentile as the range. Days with a daily maximum temperature of 35 °C or more (CCKP's hd35, Tmax >= 35 °C). 20-year averages: 1995–2014 from the historical runs; 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Projections, not forecasts of any one year.
scope.geography: Each state, province or other first-level region as CCKP draws it on the World Bank's official boundaries: the area-weighted mean of the 0.25° grid cells inside it, averaged over the land, not weighted by where people live. Left out: the 32 areas the World Bank assigns to no country, and the three units CCKP lists under China for Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, places with their own values in the country indicator, and their own region where CCKP lists one.

unit.label: days a year with a daily maximum temperature of 35 °C or more

The World Bank: Climate Change Knowledge Portal: Projected Climate Data, CMIP6 0.25-Degree (doi:10.57966/b54h-7s87): CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (World Climate Research Programme).
provenance.description: Nights a year that stay at 26 °C or more, 1995–2014 as the models simulate it and projected for 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under low, middle and very high emissions, for every country and territory, from the CMIP6 climate models as bias-corrected, downscaled and aggregated by the World Bank's Climate Change Knowledge Portal. Each value is averaged over the land of the place, not weighted by where people live. The value is the median of the models and the range runs from the 10th to the 90th percentile of the models. The 1995–2014 values are the models' simulation of the recent past, not observations.

processing.description: Read CCKP's 39 CMIP6 0.25° all_countries_subnationals files of tr26 (climatology): the multi-model ensemble median, 10th and 90th percentiles for the 1995–2014 historical runs and 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Every file holds the same 246 countries and 3,527 regions.

Checked every country's value against its own regions' values in the same file: within the lowest and highest region (±0.01, rounding), or equal to its one region. It holds for every country in every file.

Published 3,492 states, provinces and other first-level regions under CCKP's own codes, leaving out the 32 DIS.* units (areas the World Bank assigns to no country), and the 3 units CCKP lists under China for Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan (CHN.147295925 'Taiwan Sheng'; CHN.1491879 'Macau, SAR'; CHN.33364910 'Hong Kong, SAR'), places this site publishes under their own codes: the median as the value and the 10th and 90th percentiles as the range, as printed, with the 20-year window as the period and the emissions scenario as a dimension.

scope.basis: CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (bias-corrected and downscaled to 0.25° by CCKP): the median of the models, with their 10th–90th percentile as the range. Days whose minimum temperature stays at 26 °C or more (CCKP's tr26, tropical nights, T-min >= 26 °C). 20-year averages: 1995–2014 from the historical runs; 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Projections, not forecasts of any one year.
scope.geography: Each state, province or other first-level region as CCKP draws it on the World Bank's official boundaries: the area-weighted mean of the 0.25° grid cells inside it, averaged over the land, not weighted by where people live. Left out: the 32 areas the World Bank assigns to no country, and the three units CCKP lists under China for Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, places with their own values in the country indicator, and their own region where CCKP lists one.

indicators.title: Nights a year that stay at 26 °C or more by state or province, projected for 20-year windows to 2099 (CMIP6, World Bank CCKP)

unit.label: nights a year with a daily minimum temperature of 26 °C or more

provenance.attribution: The World Bank: Climate Change Knowledge Portal: Observed Climate Data, ERA5 0.25-Degree (doi:10.57966/128g-6s70): Copernicus Climate Change Service ERA5. The World Bank: Climate Change Knowledge Portal: Projected Climate Data, CMIP6 0.25-Degree (doi:10.57966/b54h-7s87): CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (World Climate Research Programme).
provenance.description: Temperature of the hottest day of the year, 1995–2014 as the models simulate it and projected for 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under low, middle and very high emissions, for every country and territory, from the CMIP6 climate models as bias-corrected, downscaled and aggregated by the World Bank's Climate Change Knowledge Portal. Each value is averaged over the land of the place, not weighted by where people live. The value is the median of the models and the range runs from the 10th to the 90th percentile of the models. The 1995–2014 values are the models' simulation of the recent past, not observations.

processing.description: Read CCKP's 39 CMIP6 0.25° all_countries_subnationals files of txx (climatology): the multi-model ensemble median, 10th and 90th percentiles for the 1995–2014 historical runs and 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Every file holds the same 246 countries and 3,528 regions.

Checked every country's value against its own regions' values in the same file: within the lowest and highest region (±0.01, rounding), or equal to its one region. It holds for every country in every file.

Published every country and territory (246), mapping CCKP's codes to the site's entities (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes as they are, KSV, CCKP's code for Kosovo, as KOS): the median as the value and the 10th and 90th percentiles as the range, as printed, with the 20-year window as the period and the emissions scenario as a dimension.

scope.basis: CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (bias-corrected and downscaled to 0.25° by CCKP): the median of the models, with their 10th–90th percentile as the range. The year's highest daily maximum temperature (CCKP's txx), averaged over the 20 years. 20-year averages: 1995–2014 from the historical runs; 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Projections, not forecasts of any one year.
scope.geography: Each country or territory as drawn by the World Bank's official boundaries: the area-weighted mean of the 0.25° grid cells inside it, averaged over the land, not weighted by where people live. No world value.

indicators.title: Temperature of the hottest day of the year by country, projected for 20-year windows to 2099 (CMIP6, World Bank CCKP)

unit.label: degrees Celsius on the hottest day of the year

provenance.attribution: The World Bank: Climate Change Knowledge Portal: Observed Climate Data, ERA5 0.25-Degree (doi:10.57966/128g-6s70): Copernicus Climate Change Service ERA5. The World Bank: Climate Change Knowledge Portal: Projected Climate Data, CMIP6 0.25-Degree (doi:10.57966/b54h-7s87): CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (World Climate Research Programme).
provenance.description: Temperature of the hottest day of the year, 1995–2014 as the models simulate it and projected for 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under low, middle and very high emissions, for every state or province, from the CMIP6 climate models as bias-corrected, downscaled and aggregated by the World Bank's Climate Change Knowledge Portal. Each value is averaged over the land of the place, not weighted by where people live. The value is the median of the models and the range runs from the 10th to the 90th percentile of the models. The 1995–2014 values are the models' simulation of the recent past, not observations.

provenance.description: Longest dry spell of the year, 1995–2014 as the models simulate it and projected for 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under low, middle and very high emissions, for every country and territory, from the CMIP6 climate models as bias-corrected, downscaled and aggregated by the World Bank's Climate Change Knowledge Portal. Each value is averaged over the land of the place, not weighted by where people live. The value is the median of the models and the range runs from the 10th to the 90th percentile of the models. The 1995–2014 values are the models' simulation of the recent past, not observations.

processing.description: Read CCKP's 39 CMIP6 0.25° all_countries_subnationals files of cdd (climatology): the multi-model ensemble median, 10th and 90th percentiles for the 1995–2014 historical runs and 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Every file holds the same 246 countries and 3,529 regions.

Checked every country's value against its own regions' values in the same file: within the lowest and highest region (±0.01, rounding), or equal to its one region. Declared exceptions, whose national values are published as CCKP prints them, each allowed to lie at most 1.53 days outside its regions' range: 19 countries (BEL, BES, BHR, BIH, BLR, CYM, DNK, FIN, GGY, JEY, KWT, LIE, LTU, LUX, NLD, QAT, SPM, VCT, VIR, CCKP's codes). In these files 46 of their values lie outside, 21 below the lowest region and 25 above the highest, by up to 1.53 days (QAT, ssp126 2020 p90: 252.88 against 254.41 to 261.66). That fits how CCKP describes its ensemble, "calculated from the individual model series": if each area's median and percentiles are taken over the models' own values for that area, a country's median need not lie between the medians of its regions, by a little and either way.

Published every country and territory (246), mapping CCKP's codes to the site's entities (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes as they are, KSV, CCKP's code for Kosovo, as KOS): the median as the value and the 10th and 90th percentiles as the range, as printed, with the 20-year window as the period and the emissions scenario as a dimension.

scope.basis: CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (bias-corrected and downscaled to 0.25° by CCKP): the median of the models, with their 10th–90th percentile as the range. The year's longest run of consecutive dry days, days with less than 1 mm of precipitation (CCKP's cdd), averaged over the 20 years. A dry spell, not a drought. 20-year averages: 1995–2014 from the historical runs; 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Projections, not forecasts of any one year.
scope.geography: Each country or territory as drawn by the World Bank's official boundaries: the area-weighted mean of the 0.25° grid cells inside it, averaged over the land, not weighted by where people live. No world value.

indicators.title: Longest dry spell of the year by country, projected for 20-year windows to 2099 (CMIP6, World Bank CCKP)

unit.label: days in the year's longest run of days with less than 1 mm of precipitation

processing.description: Read CCKP's 39 CMIP6 0.25° all_countries_subnationals files of cdd (climatology): the multi-model ensemble median, 10th and 90th percentiles for the 1995–2014 historical runs and 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Every file holds the same 246 countries and 3,529 regions.

Checked every country's value against its own regions' values in the same file: within the lowest and highest region (±0.01, rounding), or equal to its one region. Declared exceptions, whose national values are published as CCKP prints them, each allowed to lie at most 1.53 days outside its regions' range: 19 countries (BEL, BES, BHR, BIH, BLR, CYM, DNK, FIN, GGY, JEY, KWT, LIE, LTU, LUX, NLD, QAT, SPM, VCT, VIR, CCKP's codes). In these files 46 of their values lie outside, 21 below the lowest region and 25 above the highest, by up to 1.53 days (QAT, ssp126 2020 p90: 252.88 against 254.41 to 261.66). That fits how CCKP describes its ensemble, "calculated from the individual model series": if each area's median and percentiles are taken over the models' own values for that area, a country's median need not lie between the medians of its regions, by a little and either way.

Published 3,495 states, provinces and other first-level regions under CCKP's own codes, leaving out the 32 DIS.* units (areas the World Bank assigns to no country), and the 2 units CCKP lists under China for Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan (CHN.1491879 'Macau, SAR'; CHN.33364910 'Hong Kong, SAR'), places this site publishes under their own codes: the median as the value and the 10th and 90th percentiles as the range, as printed, with the 20-year window as the period and the emissions scenario as a dimension.

scope.basis: CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (bias-corrected and downscaled to 0.25° by CCKP): the median of the models, with their 10th–90th percentile as the range. The year's longest run of consecutive dry days, days with less than 1 mm of precipitation (CCKP's cdd), averaged over the 20 years. A dry spell, not a drought. 20-year averages: 1995–2014 from the historical runs; 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Projections, not forecasts of any one year.
scope.geography: Each state, province or other first-level region as CCKP draws it on the World Bank's official boundaries: the area-weighted mean of the 0.25° grid cells inside it, averaged over the land, not weighted by where people live. Left out: the 32 areas the World Bank assigns to no country, and the three units CCKP lists under China for Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, places with their own values in the country indicator, and their own region where CCKP lists one.

indicators.title: Longest dry spell of the year by state or province, projected for 20-year windows to 2099 (CMIP6, World Bank CCKP)

unit.label: days in the year's longest run of days with less than 1 mm of precipitation

provenance.attribution: The World Bank: Climate Change Knowledge Portal: Observed Climate Data, ERA5 0.25-Degree (doi:10.57966/128g-6s70): Copernicus Climate Change Service ERA5. The World Bank: Climate Change Knowledge Portal: Projected Climate Data, CMIP6 0.25-Degree (doi:10.57966/b54h-7s87): CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (World Climate Research Programme).
provenance.description: Warming from 1995–2014, projected for 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under low, middle and very high emissions, for every country and territory, from the CMIP6 climate models as bias-corrected, downscaled and aggregated by the World Bank's Climate Change Knowledge Portal. Each value is averaged over the land of the place, not weighted by where people live. The value is the median of the models and the range runs from the 10th to the 90th percentile of the models.

processing.description: Read CCKP's 36 CMIP6 0.25° all_countries_subnationals files of tas (anomaly): the multi-model ensemble median, 10th and 90th percentiles for 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099 under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5. Every file holds the same 246 countries and 3,527 regions.

Checked every country's value against its own regions' values in the same file: within the lowest and highest region (±0.01, rounding), or equal to its one region. Declared exceptions, whose national values are published as CCKP prints them, each allowed to lie at most 0.08 °C outside its regions' range: 23 countries (AUS, BES, CAN, CYP, ETH, FIN, GMB, GNB, GTM, HRV, KGZ, MNG, NAM, NER, RWA, SHN, SLE, TGO, TJK, TKM, UMI, USA, UZB, CCKP's codes). In these files 31 of their values lie outside, 14 below the lowest region and 17 above the highest, by up to 0.08 °C (KGZ, ssp245 2060 p90: 3.23 against 3.31 to 3.61). That fits how CCKP describes its ensemble, "calculated from the individual model series": if each area's median and percentiles are taken over the models' own values for that area, a country's median need not lie between the medians of its regions, by a little and either way.

Published every country and territory (246), mapping CCKP's codes to the site's entities (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes as they are, KSV, CCKP's code for Kosovo, as KOS): the median as the value and the 10th and 90th percentiles as the range, as printed, with the 20-year window as the period and the emissions scenario as a dimension.

scope.baseline: 1995–2014 mean of the same model runs (CCKP's reference period)
scope.basis: CMIP6 multi-model ensemble (bias-corrected and downscaled to 0.25° by CCKP): the median of the models, with their 10th–90th percentile as the range. Projections, not forecasts of any one year.
scope.geography: Each country or territory as drawn by the World Bank's official boundaries: the area-weighted mean of the 0.25° grid cells inside it, averaged over the land, not weighted by where people live. No world value.

processing.description: Read the sheet 'GHG_per_capita_by_country' of EDGAR_2026_GHG_booklet_2026.xlsx (sha256 bb77a0da5735…): one row per country or aggregate, one column per year 1970–2025, in tonnes of CO₂-equivalent per person per year (t CO2eq/cap/yr) as the workbook's info sheet states. Each value is published exactly as stored in its cell: nothing is rounded, added up, divided or converted, because the licence of the fossil CO₂ part (IEA-EDGAR CO2, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0) allows no derivatives.

Matched EDGAR's codes to ours: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes directly, except GLOBAL TOTAL "GLOBAL TOTAL" is WLD, EU27 "EU27" is EU27, ANT "Curaçao" is CUW, SCG "Serbia and Montenegro" is SRB_MNE (ANT is the old code of the Netherlands Antilles; EDGAR names the row Curaçao, here and on its report profile; SCG is one row for Serbia and Montenegro together). Rows that cover a country together with a neighbour (CHE "Switzerland and Liechtenstein", ESP "Spain and Andorra", FRA "France and Monaco", ISR "Israel and Palestine, State of", ITA "Italy, San Marino and the Holy See", SDN "Sudan and South Sudan") are published under the code EDGAR gives them, with EDGAR's row name as a note on every value.

Checked against the report PDF (sha256 4e5712706aed…): the totals exclude land use, land-use change and forestry (page 11: 'The latest EDGAR estimates indicate that global GHG emissions (excluding LULUCF) reached a new record high of 54.1 Gt CO₂eq in 2025'), and the world total includes international shipping and aviation (page 74: 'Global totals for all countries, including international shipping and aviation').

Values for 2024 and 2025 are marked preliminary, because the report says (page 50) 'the emissions for the Fast-Track years (2024-2025) reported in this booklet will be updated in subsequent editions of this booklet'.
